definition_zh: 创新；革新；（新）方法、新事物
definition_en: a new idea, method, or product, or the act of creating such new things
core_image: 旧机器旁边摆出一台从没见过的新装置，围着看的人抄下了图纸
scene: 老厂房里摆着一排用了多年的旧设备，墙角却多了一台新样机。The engineer called the new design a real innovation, not just a small repair.
sceneCN: 这里 innovation 是「创新、新东西」（第 1 个义项：全新的想法、方法或产品），句意为工程师说这项新设计是真正的创新，而不只是一次小修小补。画面里的物件：旧设备、新样机、图纸。

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「创新的；有新意的」
由拉丁词干构成的后备动词，义为「革新；创新」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「创新者；革新者」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「与创新有关的」

senses.title: A new idea or method
senses.definition: a new idea, method, or device, especially one that changes how something is done
senses.definitionCN: 尤指改变了做事方式的新想法、新方法或新装置
senses.example: The online booking system was a real innovation for the small hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 网上预订系统对这家小旅馆来说是真正的创新。
senses.why: Latin novus means new; in- makes it "into the new", so an innovation is something brought into the world as new.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 novus 意为「新的」；in- 使之成为「进入新奇状态」，所以 innovation 是被带进世界的新东西。

senses.title: The act of bringing in new things
senses.definition: the activity of introducing new ideas or methods into a business, school, or industry
senses.definitionCN: 把新想法或新方法引入企业、学校或行业的行为
senses.example: Innovation is what keeps a small company alive in a crowded market.
senses.exampleCN: 创新是让小公司在拥挤的市场中活下来的东西。
senses.why: The noun also names the doing, not only the thing done: it is the process of stepping into the new.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也指「做的过程」而不只是「做成的东西」：它就是走进新事物的过程。

senses.title: A new product on the market
senses.definition: a product or service that is new to the market and often credited to one company
senses.definitionCN: 市场上新出现、往往归功于某家公司的新产品或新服务
senses.example: Their latest innovation is a battery that charges in minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们最新的革新产品是一种几分钟就能充满电的电池。
senses.why: From the busy workshop it moved to the shop window: each launch is presented as an innovation.
senses.whyCN: 从忙碌的车间走到了橱窗：每一次新品发布都被称为一项 innovation。

senses.title: A change in long-standing habits
senses.definition: a change in well-established customs or habits, sometimes unwelcome at first
senses.definitionCN: 对由来已久的习惯或风俗所做的改变，起初常不受欢迎
senses.example: Replacing the paper register with an app was an innovation nobody asked for.
senses.exampleCN: 用一个应用取代纸质登记簿，是没人要求过的改变。
senses.why: The oldest examples refer to novelties in religion and law, where a new practice always disturbed someone.
senses.whyCN: 最早的例子指宗教与法律上的新做法，新的做法总会惊动某些人。

intro.en: Innovation is a Latin noun of action built on novus "new"; English took it through French in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: innovation 是以拉丁语 novus「新的」为基础的拉丁语行为名词，中世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective novus "new" is old Latin and related to the adverb novus-derived nunc "now".
items.cn: 形容词 novus「新的」是古老的拉丁词，与表示「现在」的 nunc 有渊源。

items.en: Novare "to make new" yielded the verb innovare, literally "to make new in".
items.cn: novare「使变新」生出动词 innovare，字面是「使里面变新」。

items.en: The abstract noun innovatio "a renewing" was used in late Latin, chiefly for renewal of laws.
items.cn: 抽象名词 innovatio「更新」见于晚期拉丁语，主要用于法律的更新。

items.en: Old French innovacion carried the word into everyday speech during the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 中世纪时古法语 innovacion 把这个词带入日常言语。

items.en: From the sixteenth century it named any new practice; business writing later made it a slogan.
items.cn: 十六世纪起它泛指任何新做法；后来的商业写作又让它成为口号。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for "new"; the near-meaning group holds other words for change and novelty.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「新」这一词根；近义组收其他表示「改变、新事物」的词。

entries.definition: A story; as an adjective, new and unusual, built on Latin novus.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「小说」，作形容词义为「新颖的」，都基于拉丁语 novus。

entries.definition: The quality of being new, or a small new object sold for fun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「新奇；新奇小玩意」，词根同是「新」。

entries.definition: To make an old building new again, with the prefix re- "again".
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「翻新」，前缀 re- 表「再次」，词根仍是「新」。

entries.definition: Something created for the first time, often a device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发明」，指首次创造出的东西，常指装置。

entries.definition: A change that repairs a system rather than creating something new.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改革」，指修补制度而非创造新事物。

entries.definition: A sudden important advance, stronger in tone than innovation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「突破」，语气比 innovation 更强，强调突然的重要进展。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin root nov- "new" and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用拉丁词根 nov-「新」以及这个词真实的搭配。

normal.en: nov- is new: innovation is the new thing brought in.
normal.cn: nov- 就是「新」：innovation 就是被带进来的新东西。

normal.en: The same root gives novel, novelty and renovate.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 novel、novelty、renovate。

normal.en: Tech firms live or die by technological innovation.
normal.cn: 科技公司的生死取决于技术创新。

normal.en: An innovation is judged by users, not by its inventor.
normal.cn: 创新由用户评判，而不是由发明者评判。

normal.en: Small innovations often beat one big invention.
normal.cn: 许多小创新往往胜过一件大发明。

abstract.en: Think of a door marked in- that opens into a room called new.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着 in- 的门，通向一个叫「新」的房间。

abstract.en: An innovation is a habit the world has not yet learned.
abstract.cn: 创新是世界尚未学会的一种习惯。

abstract.en: Every innovation starts as someone else's odd idea.
abstract.cn: 每一项创新最初都是别人眼里的怪想法。

examples.en: The factory owes its survival to steady innovation.
examples.cn: 这家工厂靠持续创新才得以存活。

examples.en: Cheap solar panels were the decade's biggest innovation.
examples.cn: 廉价太阳能板是那十年最大的创新。

examples.en: Teachers were asked to share one innovation at the meeting.
examples.cn: 会上要求老师们各分享一项创新做法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一脑维新」——一脑子的维新想法，就是创新

root: 拉丁语 novus「新的」→ novare「使变新」→ innovare「使里面变新」→ 晚期拉丁语抽象名词 innovatio「更新」，中世纪经古法语 innovacion 进入英语。nov-「新」也见于 novel、novelty、renovate。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the new thing, the act of making it, the product sold, and the change imposed on old habits.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：新东西本身、制造新东西的行为、售卖的新产品，以及强加于旧习惯的改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something never seen before is brought in and set beside the old.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件从未见过的东西被带进来，摆在旧东西旁边。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: a new method enters the way work is done.
branches.cn: 车间这条线：新方法进入做事的流程。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: innovation also names the ongoing act of bringing new things in.
branches.cn: 过程这条线：innovation 也指持续把新东西带进来的行为。

branches.en: THE SHOP WINDOW: the product itself is displayed as an innovation.
branches.cn: 橱窗这条线：产品本身被展示为一项创新。

branches.en: THE OLD CUSTOM: a change in habit is resisted before it is accepted.
branches.cn: 旧风俗这条线：习惯的改变先被抵制，之后才被接受。

branches.en: THE LINK: the thing and the act share the movement into the new.
branches.cn: 连接线：东西与行为共享「走进新」这一动作。

intro.en: Innovation splits into the Latin prefix in-, the root nov- "new", and the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: innovation 可拆为拉丁前缀 in-、「新」词根 nov- 与名词词尾 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus, novare and innovare are all attested, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus、novare、innovare 均有记载，只有更早的印欧形式属于重构。

items.exampleCN: 它标出朝向新状态的动作。

items.example: The root is visible in novel and renovate.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根见于 novel 与 renovate。

items.example: The adjective is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是整个词族的根基。

definition_zh: 创新的；革新的；有创意的
definition_en: introducing or using new ideas, methods, or designs
core_image: 一双手把旧图纸翻过来，背面画着完全不一样的方案
scene: 实验室的桌面上摊着旧方案和新草图。Her innovative approach to packing cut shipping costs by half.
sceneCN: 这里 innovative 是「有创意的、创新的」（第 1 个义项：引人新想法或新方法），句意为她创新的包装办法把运费降了一半。画面里能看到的物件：旧图纸、新草图、计算器。

pos.zh: 形容词：创新的；有创意的

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「创新；新事物」
同族动词，义为「革新；创新」
由词干加 -or 构成，义为「创新者」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「有创意地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「创新性」

senses.title: Introducing new ideas
senses.definition: using or introducing new ideas and original methods rather than copying old ones
senses.definitionCN: 使用或引入新想法、独创新方法，而不是照搬旧办法
senses.example: The school hired an innovative teacher who turns grammar into games.
senses.exampleCN: 学校请了一位把语法变成游戏的创新老师。
senses.why: The verb innovate plus the adjective ending -ive gives "having the quality of bringing in the new".
senses.whyCN: 动词 innovate 加上形容词词尾 -ive，得到「具有引入新事物之性质的」。

senses.title: Original and well designed
senses.definition: designed in a clever and original way, often praised for its design
senses.definitionCN: 以巧妙、独创的方式设计，常因设计受到称赞
senses.example: The lamp has an innovative folded-paper shade.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯有一个构思新颖的折纸灯罩。
senses.why: The same quality moves from methods to objects: a thing can be called innovative when its design itself is the new idea.
senses.whyCN: 同一性质从方法移到物件：当设计本身就是新想法时，这个物件也叫 innovative。

senses.title: Ahead of the market
senses.definition: working in a way that is unusually advanced for the industry at the time
senses.definitionCN: 以在当时的行业里格外先进的方式运作
senses.example: Investors look for small innovative firms before they grow famous.
senses.exampleCN: 投资人会在小公司出名之前寻找那些领先创新的小企业。
senses.why: Business writing stretched the adjective to describe companies and markets that act before their rivals do.
senses.whyCN: 商业写作把这个形容词扩用到先于对手行动的公司与市场上。

intro.en: Innovative is the noun innovation reshaped with the Latin adjective ending -ivus, which came down as English -ive.
intro.cn: innovative 是在名词 innovation 之上换用拉丁形容词词尾 -ivus（英语作 -ive）而成。

items.en: Novus "new" is the root that also gives novel and renovate.
items.cn: novus「新的」是词根，也给出 novel、renovate。

items.en: Innovare "to make new inside, renew" supplied the verb stem.
items.cn: innovare「使里面变新、更新」提供了动词词干。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives meaning "tending to do".
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 构成表示「倾向于做……」的形容词。

items.en: Innovative appears in English in the eighteenth century, first in writing about politics and trade.
items.cn: innovative 在十八世纪英语中出现，最初见于讨论政治与贸易的文字。

items.en: Twentieth-century advertising turned it into a standard word of praise for products.
items.cn: 二十世纪的广告把它变成了赞美产品的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the nov- stem; the near-meaning group holds other adjectives of newness and originality.
note.cn: 形近组共享 nov- 词干；近义组收其他表示「新」与「独创」的形容词。

entries.definition: Full of original ideas; built on the Latin root for "make", not on novus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有创造力的」，词根是拉丁语「制造」，与 novus 无关。

entries.definition: New and unusual, from the same Latin novus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「新颖的」，来自同一拉丁词 novus。

entries.definition: To renew an old building with the prefix re-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「翻新」，前缀 re- 表「再次」。

entries.definition: Good at thinking up new things, said of people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「善于发明的」，多形容人。

entries.definition: Different from anything else, not following others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「独创的」，强调与任何东西都不同。

entries.definition: A compound describing a person who thinks inventively.
entries.definitionCN: 复合形容词，形容善于创新思考的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the -ive ending to a quality you can see in a person or a design.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 -ive 词尾与能从人身上或设计中看到的性质联系起来。

normal.en: innovation is the thing, innovative is the quality that produced it.
normal.cn: innovation 是产物，innovative 是产生它的那种性质。

normal.en: The -ive ending marks an adjective of tendency, as in active and creative.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 表示倾向性的形容词，如 active、creative。

normal.en: An innovative approach often costs less than the old one.
normal.cn: 创新的办法往往比旧办法更省钱。

normal.en: Investors chase innovative firms before they are famous.
normal.cn: 投资人会在公司出名前追逐创新企业。

normal.en: Use more innovative instead of innovativer; the word takes more.
normal.cn: 比较级要用 more innovative，不能写 innovativer。

abstract.en: Think of flipping an old drawing over to find a new plan on the back.
abstract.cn: 想象把一张旧图纸翻过来，背面画着新方案。

abstract.en: Innovative is a door that opens outward, away from habit.
abstract.cn: innovative 像一扇朝外开的门，远离习惯。

abstract.en: A truly innovative idea looks strange before it looks obvious.
abstract.cn: 真正创新的想法先显得奇怪，后来才显得理所当然。

examples.en: They praised her innovative use of cheap materials.
examples.cn: 他们称赞她创新地使用了廉价材料。

examples.en: An innovative design does not always sell well.
examples.cn: 创新的设计并不总是卖得好。

examples.en: The clinic is known for its innovative treatments.
examples.cn: 这家诊所因其创新疗法而闻名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一脑维新」——脑子里总做维新，人就显得有创意

root: 由拉丁语 novus「新的」→ novare「使变新」→ innovare「更新」构成的词干，加上形容词词尾 -ivus（英语 -ive）。因此 innovative 字面是「带有更新倾向的」，与 innovation、innovate、innovator 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: new in method, new in design, and advanced for the market.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：方法上新、设计上新，以及在市场中格外先进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old drawing is flipped over and a completely different plan shows on the back.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧图纸被翻过来，背面是完全不同的方案。

branches.en: THE METHOD: teaching, packing or working in a new way.
branches.cn: 方法这条线：用新方式教学、包装或工作。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a clever design can carry the adjective itself.
branches.cn: 物件这条线：巧妙的设计本身就能承载这个形容词。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a company acts before its rivals and is called innovative.
branches.cn: 市场这条线：公司先于对手行动，被称为创新。

branches.en: THE LINK: whether person, method or object, the quality is the same.
branches.cn: 连接线：不论是人、方法还是物件，性质是同一个。

branches.en: THE TONE: the word is almost always praise in advertising.
branches.cn: 语气线：在广告里这个词几乎总是褒义。

intro.en: Innovative is innovat- plus the Latin adjective ending -ivus, English -ive.
intro.cn: innovative 由 innovat- 加拉丁形容词词尾 -ivus（英语 -ive）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms novus, novare and innovare are attested; the suffix -ivus is a regular adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus、novare、innovare 都有记载，-ivus 是规则的形容词词尾。

scene: 这里指「无机的」。 The geologist ruled out any biological origin and logged the crust as an inorganic deposit.

senses.title: Chemistry without carbon
senses.titleCN: 无机化学：不以碳骨架为中心的化合物
senses.definition: describing chemical compounds that are not built on carbon chains or rings, the traditional dividing line of inorganic chemistry
senses.definitionCN: 指不以碳链或碳环为骨架的化合物，这是无机化学与传统有机化学的分界
senses.example: Inorganic chemistry covers salts, metals, acids and coordination compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 无机化学研究盐类、金属、酸以及配位化合物。
senses.why: The prefix in- negates organic, and organic chemistry was defined in the nineteenth century as the chemistry of carbon compounds, so everything outside that family became inorganic.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定 organic；19 世纪把有机化学界定为碳化合物的化学，于是不属于这一族的东西统统被叫作无机。

senses.title: Not made by living things
senses.titleCN: 非生物来源：不经过生命过程形成
senses.definition: formed by physical or chemical processes alone, with no involvement of plants, animals or microbes
senses.definitionCN: 仅由物理或化学过程形成，没有植物、动物或微生物参与
senses.example: The crystals grew by purely inorganic processes in the cave water.
senses.exampleCN: 这些晶体在洞穴水里完全靠无机过程生长出来。
senses.why: The chemical division was extended to origins: what living bodies build is organic, what rock and water build is inorganic.
senses.whyCN: 化学上的分界被推广到成因：生物体建造的属有机，岩石与水建造的属无机。

senses.title: Mineral ions in nutrition
senses.titleCN: 无机养分：植物吸收的矿质离子
senses.definition: in biology, the mineral salts and ions that plants and animals take up, as opposed to carbon-based food molecules
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指动植物吸收的矿质盐与离子，与含碳的食物分子相对
senses.example: Plants absorb inorganic ions such as nitrate, phosphate and potassium from the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 植物从土壤中吸收硝酸根、磷酸根、钾等无机离子。
senses.why: Nutrient studies separate the mineral ions a plant takes from the organic compounds it builds, so the adjective marks the raw mineral input.
senses.whyCN: 养分研究把植物吸收的矿质离子与它合成的有机化合物分开，这个形容词就标出未加工的矿物输入。

senses.title: Abiotic origin in geology
senses.titleCN: 地质无机成因：不经生物而形成的矿藏
senses.definition: in earth science, describing deposits or hydrocarbons whose origin is argued to be abiotic rather than biological
senses.definitionCN: 地球科学中指其成因被主张为非生物而非生物的沉积物或碳氢化合物
senses.example: The debate over inorganic petroleum asks whether oil can form without buried organisms.
senses.exampleCN: 关于无机石油的争论，追问的是石油能否不经埋藏的生物体而形成。
senses.why: The word lets geologists state a contested claim in one adjective: the material exists, but its source is not life.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词让地质学家用一个词表明有争议的主张：物质确实存在，但来源不是生命。

senses.title: Inorganic business growth
senses.titleCN: 外延式增长：靠并购而非自身经营扩大
senses.definition: in business, growth achieved by buying other firms or assets rather than by expanding existing operations
senses.definitionCN: 商业上指通过收购其他公司或资产、而非扩大自身经营获得的增长
senses.example: The group's expansion was largely inorganic, driven by a string of acquisitions.
senses.exampleCN: 该集团的扩张基本是外延式的，靠一连串收购推动。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the living metaphor: organic growth grows from within like a body, while inorganic growth is assembled from outside parts.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了生物学隐喻：organic growth 像身体一样从内部生长，inorganic growth 则像从外部拼装零件。

senses.title: Lacking living structure
senses.titleCN: 无生命结构：不会自我修复的整体
senses.definition: having no organised living structure, so that damage is permanent and no self-repair occurs
senses.definitionCN: 没有有组织的生命结构，因而损伤不可逆、不会自我修复
senses.example: An inorganic body cannot heal itself, so every crack stays where it formed.
senses.exampleCN: 无生命的物体无法自愈，因此每一道裂缝都会留在原处。
senses.why: This is the plain negation of the biological sense: whatever a living body does by organisation, an inorganic body cannot do.
senses.whyCN: 这是生物学义项的直接否定：生命体靠组织结构做到的事，无机物体一件也做不到。

senses.title: Non-biodegradable waste
senses.titleCN: 无机废弃物：不能靠微生物分解
senses.definition: in waste management, material such as glass, metal or plastic that microbes cannot break down
senses.definitionCN: 废弃物管理中指玻璃、金属、塑料这类微生物无法分解的材料
senses.example: Inorganic waste such as glass and metal can be recycled instead of landfilled.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃、金属这类无机废弃物可以回收，而不必填埋。
senses.why: Because decomposition is a biological process, materials that resist it are grouped as inorganic regardless of their chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 由于分解是生物过程，抵抗分解的材料就被归为无机，尽管其化学构成未必如此。

senses.title: Hard form in art and design
senses.titleCN: 无机形态：几何、坚硬、不带生命曲线
senses.definition: in art and design criticism, describing shapes that are angular and lifeless rather than flowing and bodily
senses.definitionCN: 艺术与设计批评中指棱角分明、没有生命感而非流畅有机的形态
senses.example: Her later sculptures moved from organic curves to hard inorganic geometry.
senses.exampleCN: 她后期的雕塑从有机曲线转向坚硬的无机几何形态。
senses.why: Critics borrowed the adjective to contrast two families of form, so a welded plate can be called inorganic without any claim about chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 批评家借用这个形容词来对照两类形态，因此一块焊接钢板也可以被称作无机的，而不涉及任何化学判断。

intro.en: Inorganic is the negative of organic, and organic descends from Greek organon 'tool, instrument, bodily organ'. The chemistry sense is a nineteenth-century narrowing of the word.
intro.cn: inorganic 是 organic 的否定形式，而 organic 出自希腊语 organon「工具、器械、身体器官」。化学义是 19 世纪对词义的收窄。

items.en: Greek organon named a tool or implement and, in medicine and philosophy, an organ of the body. It is built on ergon 'work', so the underlying picture is an instrument for doing work.
items.cn: 希腊语 organon 指工具或器械，在医学与哲学中也指身体器官。它由 ergon「工作」构成，底层意象是「用于做工的器具」。

items.en: Latin took the word as organum, used for an instrument and later for a musical instrument. The adjective organicus appears in later Latin with the sense 'instrumental'.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 organum，指器具，后也指乐器。后期拉丁语中出现形容词 organicus，意为「器具的、工具性的」。

items.en: English organic appears around 1600, first meaning 'relating to bodily organs', then 'belonging to living things'. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 organic 约在 1600 年出现，最初意为「与身体器官有关的」，随后转为「属于生物的」。最早的确切书证存疑。

items.en: Around the 1840s chemists fixed a boundary: organic compounds contain carbon and were once thought to require a living force, while mineral compounds do not. Inorganic was coined for the second class.
items.cn: 约 1840 年代，化学家确定了一条界线：有机化合物含碳、曾被认为需要「生命力」参与，矿物化合物则不需要。inorganic 就是为后一类造的词。

items.en: When Wohler made urea from ammonium cyanate in 1828, the idea that organic compounds required life began to collapse, yet the chemical label organic survived and inorganic stayed its partner.
items.cn: 1828 年维勒用氰酸铵合成尿素后，「有机化合物必须有生命参与」的观念开始瓦解，但 organic 这一化学标签保留下来，inorganic 也随之成为它的对偶。

items.en: The exact person who first wrote inorganic in its chemical sense is not recorded, and the first English date is uncertain; it is usually placed in the 1840s but the citation is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：最先以化学义使用 inorganic 的人并无记载，英语首见年代存疑，通常定在 1840 年代，但书证并不确定。

note.en: The first group holds words that look alike but divide the world differently; the second holds near-synonyms for 'not alive' that are often used loosely.
note.cn: 第一组是形近但划分世界方式不同的词；第二组是常被宽泛替换的「非生命」近义词。

entries.definition: Means carbon-based in chemistry, coming from living things, or grown without synthetic chemicals in farming. It is not simply the antonym of artificial.
entries.definitionCN: 化学上指含碳的，也指来自生物的，或农业上不用合成化学品的。它并不等于「人造」的反义词。

entries.definition: Used mainly for food grown without organic certification. It says nothing about carbon compounds, so it is not a chemical term.
entries.definitionCN: 主要用于未经有机认证生产的食品。它不涉及碳化合物，因此不是化学术语。

entries.definition: Names a natural inorganic solid with a definite structure. All minerals are inorganic in origin, but many inorganic substances, such as table salt in solution, are not minerals.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有确定结构的天然无机固体。矿物在成因上都是无机的，但许多无机物（如溶解的食盐）并不是矿物。

entries.definition: Describes a process or factor with no biological component. It overlaps with inorganic origin but is used of environments and factors, not of substances.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不含生物成分的过程或因素。它与无机成因重叠，但多用于环境与因素，而不是具体物质。

entries.definition: Means 'not alive' and can describe a stone, a robot or a dull party. It says nothing about chemical composition, unlike inorganic.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「无生命的」，可形容石头、机器人或沉闷的聚会。与 inorganic 不同，它完全不涉及化学组成。

entries.definition: Means produced by chemical synthesis rather than extracted from nature. A synthetic compound may be organic, so it is not a synonym of inorganic.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过化学合成而非从自然中提取得到的。合成化合物也可能是有机的，因此它不是 inorganic 的同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'not' + organic: the chemistry of everything that is not carbon-based.
normal.cn: in-「不」+ organic：研究一切不以碳为骨架之物的化学。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organic, organism, organize, organization and organelle.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organic、organism、organize、organization、organelle。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: inorganic chemistry, inorganic compound, inorganic fertilizer, inorganic waste.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：无机化学、无机化合物、无机肥料、无机废弃物。

normal.en: Organic means carbon-based in chemistry and certified in farming; inorganic is the chemical opposite only.
normal.cn: organic 在化学上指含碳、在农业上指获认证；inorganic 只是化学上的对立面。

normal.en: Wohler's urea synthesis in 1828 ended the belief that organic compounds needed a living force.
normal.cn: 1828 年维勒合成尿素，终结了「有机化合物需要生命力」的信念。

abstract.en: Picture a salt crystal growing in dark water, with no leaf, no cell and no seed anywhere near it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚盐晶在暗处的水中生长，周围没有叶子、没有细胞、也没有种子。

abstract.en: Picture a company bought whole and bolted on, adding size without growing a single new customer of its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一家公司被整体买下、拼接进来，规模变大了，却没有自己长出一个新客户。

abstract.en: Picture a welded steel sculpture: hard angles, no curve that suggests a body.
abstract.cn: 想象一件焊接钢雕：棱角坚硬，没有一处曲线暗示身体。

examples.en: Inorganic salts dissolved in the lake water raise its mineral content.
examples.cn: 溶解在湖水中的无机盐提高了它的矿物含量。

examples.en: The lab keeps organic and inorganic samples in separate cabinets.
examples.cn: 实验室把有机样品与无机样品存放在不同的柜子里。

examples.en: Investors questioned whether the company's inorganic growth could be sustained.
examples.cn: 投资者质疑这家公司的外延式增长能否持续。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（不）+ organic（有机的）」——不属于生命与碳化学的东西 → inorganic 无机的

root: 拉丁 in-「不」+ 希腊 organon「器官、工具」→ 英语 organic；19 世纪化学把不含碳的化合物称作 inorganic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one negation: the word first removes carbon from chemistry, then removes life from origin, then removes inner organisation from growth, waste and form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条否定线展开：先把碳从化学中拿掉，再把生命从成因中拿掉，最后把内在组织性从增长、废弃物与形态中拿掉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mineral crust with no leaf, no cell and no seed anywhere near it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层矿物结壳，周围没有叶子、没有细胞、也没有种子。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: carbon is the dividing line, so salts, metals and acids are inorganic.
branches.cn: 化学分界：碳是界线，因此盐、金属与酸都属无机。

branches.en: ORIGIN: the same line is drawn through time, asking whether life took part in forming the material.
branches.cn: 成因：同一条界线沿时间延伸，追问生命是否参与了物质的形成。

branches.en: RAW INPUT: plants absorb mineral ions as inorganic nutrients before building organic matter.
branches.cn: 原料输入：植物先吸收作为无机养分的矿质离子，再合成有机物。

branches.en: EXTERNAL GROWTH: business borrows the biology, so buying a firm is inorganic and adding customers is organic.
branches.cn: 外部增长：商业借用生物学说法，收购公司属无机，新增客户属有机。

branches.en: LIFELESS MATTER: no self-repair, no decomposition and no organic curve all follow from the same missing organisation.
branches.cn: 无生命物质：不会自愈、不会被分解、没有有机曲线，都源于同一种「缺少组织性」。

intro.en: Inorganic is a Latin negative prefix sitting on a Greek-derived adjective, so the word literally says 'not organ-like'.
intro.cn: inorganic 是拉丁否定前缀加在一个源自希腊语的形容词上，字面意思就是「不像器官的」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin negative prefix in- (im-, il-, ir- before certain sounds) marks absence, while organicus and organum carry the Greek organon into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁否定前缀 in-（在部分音前作 im-、il-、ir-）表示缺失，而 organicus 与 organum 把希腊语 organon 带进英语。

items.meaning: not carbon-based; not produced by life
items.meaningCN: 不含碳骨架的；非生命产生的
items.example: Inorganic pigments resist fading in sunlight.
items.exampleCN: 无机颜料在阳光下不易褪色。

items.meaning: relating to organs or to living, carbon-based matter
items.meaningCN: 与器官有关的；有机的、含碳的
items.example: Organic compounds always contain carbon-hydrogen bonds.
items.exampleCN: 有机化合物总含有碳氢键。

items.meaning: a body part with a function; also an instrument
items.meaningCN: 具有特定功能的器官；也指乐器或机构
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.meaning: a living body made of coordinated parts
items.meaningCN: 由协调运作的各部分构成的生物体
items.example: A single-celled organism still counts as life.
items.exampleCN: 单细胞生物仍然算作生命。

items.meaning: to arrange parts into a working whole
items.meaningCN: 把各部分安排成可运作的整体
items.example: She organized the files by project.

items.meaning: the act of arranging; a structured body
items.meaningCN: 安排的行为；有结构的团体
items.example: The organization employs forty researchers.
items.exampleCN: 该机构雇用了四十名研究人员。

items.meaning: a small functional structure inside a cell
items.meaningCN: 细胞内部的小型功能结构
items.example: Mitochondria are organelles that release energy.
items.exampleCN: 线粒体是释放能量的细胞器。

items.meaningCN: 研究非碳化合物的化学分支
items.example: Inorganic chemistry explains why rust forms.
items.exampleCN: 无机化学解释了铁锈为何生成。

latinEntries.structure: in- (negative prefix, assimilated to im-, il-, ir-)
organum, organi (n., second declension; from Greek organon)
organicus (adj., later Latin; from Greek organikos)

definition_zh: 输入；投入（资源、意见）；输入端；输入数据
definition_en: something put into a system, such as data, effort, or money, or the act of putting it in
core_image: 一只手把数据卡片推进机器的进料口
scene: 技术员坐在电脑前核对屏幕上的一行行数字。The new software needs less input from the user.
sceneCN: 这里 input 是「输入」（第 1 个义项：输入系统的数据或指令）；句意为新软件需要的用户输入更少。图中可辨识物件：键盘、屏幕、数据卡。

pos.zh: 名词：输入；投入；输入端；输入数据

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 device 构成，义为「输入设备」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「数据录入」
由前缀 out- 构成的对应词，义为「输出」

senses.title: Data put into a computer
senses.definition: information or instructions put into a computer or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 送入计算机或机器的信息或指令
senses.example: The program waits for input from the keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 程序等待来自键盘的输入。
senses.why: Input is the noun of putting in: whatever is pushed into a system through its entrance.
senses.whyCN: input 是「put in」的名词：凡经入口推送进系统的东西。

senses.title: Effort or resources put in
senses.definition: the effort, money, advice, or time given to a project, often by several people
senses.definitionCN: 投入某项工程的努力、资金、建议或时间，常由多方提供
senses.example: The report was written with input from every department.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是在各部门的意见基础上写成的。
senses.why: Factories speak of inputs of labour and materials, and meetings of inputs of advice.
senses.whyCN: 工厂说劳动与材料的投入，会议说建议的投入。

senses.title: The terminal that receives data
senses.definition: a place or device through which signals enter a system
senses.definitionCN: 信号进入系统的位置或装置
senses.example: Plug the cable into the audio input.
senses.exampleCN: 把线插进音频输入口。
senses.why: The entrance point takes the name of what passes through it.
senses.whyCN: 入口处往往就以流经它的东西命名。

intro.en: Input is not Latin at all: it is put with the prefix in- on the English model of output.
intro.cn: input 完全不是拉丁词：它是英语把 put 加前缀 in- 造出的词，与 output 对应。

items.en: Put has no certain origin even in Old English, where it appears in place names.
items.cn: put 连在古英语中也来源不明，只在地名里出现。

items.en: Input was formed in the eighteenth century for money and resources put into a business.
items.cn: input 在十八世纪造出，指投入企业的资金与资源。

items.en: Engineers took up the word for power and signals feeding a machine.
items.cn: 十九世纪工程师用它指供给机器的动力与信号。

items.en: Computing fixed the sense of data entered into a system, and output grew beside it.
items.cn: 计算机业固定了「输入数据」的义项，output 随之而来。

items.en: Everyday speech extended it to advice and effort contributed by people.
items.cn: 日常用语又把它扩展到人们贡献的意见与努力。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words made with put and with the prefix in-; the near-meaning group gathers other words for contributions.
note.cn: 形近组收由 put 与 in- 构成的词；近义组收表示「贡献」的其他词。

entries.definition: What a system produces, the opposite of input.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「输出」，与 input 相对。

entries.definition: The act of entering data.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据录入」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: To bring goods into a country, with a Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「进口」，形近但词源不同。

entries.definition: Something given to a shared effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贡献」，指对共同努力的付出。

entries.definition: Information in a form a computer can process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据」，指可供计算机处理的信息。

entries.definition: Money or effort put in for future gain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「投资」，指为将来收益而投入的钱或力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain English build of the word, which is simply in plus put.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用这个词朴素的英语构成，即 in 加 put。

normal.en: Input is in plus put: what you put in.
normal.cn: input 就是 in 加 put：你投入进去的东西。

normal.en: Output sits on the other side of the same wall.
normal.cn: output 位于同一堵墙的另一侧。

normal.en: Ask for input before you write the report, not after.
normal.cn: 写报告之前征求意见，别等后面。

normal.en: Users type input; the computer answers with output.
normal.cn: 用户键入 input，计算机回以 output。

normal.en: An audio input is the socket that lets sound in.
normal.cn: audio input 是让声音进来的插孔。

abstract.en: Picture grain poured into a hopper: what goes in determines what comes out.
abstract.cn: 想象谷物倒进料斗：送进去的决定了出来的。

abstract.en: A system is only as good as the input it receives.
abstract.cn: 系统的质量取决于它接收的输入。

abstract.en: Every effort you put in is a kind of input, even when nobody records it.
abstract.cn: 你的每一点付出都是一种输入，即使没人记录。

examples.en: The form asks for input of your personal details.
examples.cn: 表格要求输入你的个人信息。

examples.en: We would welcome input from parents on the new timetable.
examples.cn: 新课程表方面我们欢迎家长提出意见。

examples.en: Insert the microphone into the input at the back.
examples.cn: 把麦克风插到后面的输入口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因普特」——因「普特」把数据输入了电脑

root: input 是英语用 in- + put 仿 output 构成的词，十八世纪指投入企业的资金与资源；十九世纪用于机器动力与信号，二十世纪计算机业固定为「数据输入」，后引申为「意见投入」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: data entering a machine, resources or advice entering a project, and the socket where signals enter.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：进入机器的数据、进入项目的资源与意见，以及信号进入的接口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grain is poured into a hopper; what goes in decides what comes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：谷物倒进料斗，进多少决定出多少。

branches.en: THE KEYBOARD: typing is the commonest form of input.
branches.cn: 键盘这条线：打字是最常见的 input。

branches.en: THE PROGRAM: a program cannot run without data from somewhere.
branches.cn: 程序这条线：没有数据来源，程序无法运行。

branches.en: THE MEETING: a good decision needs input from the people affected.
branches.cn: 会议这条线：好的决定需要受影响者的意见。

branches.en: THE FACTORY: labour, fuel and material are the inputs of production.
branches.cn: 工厂这条线：劳动、燃料与材料是生产的投入。

branches.en: THE SOCKET: the input is also the physical entrance.
branches.cn: 接口这条线：the input 也指物理上的入口。

intro.en: Input is a modern English compound; the prefix in- carries the sense of entering.

definition_en: a question asked to get information, or an official investigation into something
core_image: 一个人探身向前，皱着眉向对面的人发问
scene: 服务台的电话一直响个不停，值班员一一记录。We received several inquiries about the new course.
sceneCN: 这里 inquiry 是「询问」（第 1 个义项：为获得信息而提问）；句意为我们收到了几份关于新课程的询问。图中可辨识物件：电话、登记本、台灯。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀还原，义为「询问；调查」
同根形容词，义为「好问的；好奇的」
同根名词，义为「审问者」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「询问者」

senses.title: A question
senses.definition: a question you ask in order to get information
senses.definitionCN: 为获得信息而提出的问题
senses.example: She made an inquiry about train times.
senses.exampleCN: 她询问了火车时刻。
senses.why: In- "into" plus quaerere "to seek" gives "a seeking into": a question is a search for information.
senses.whyCN: in-「向内」加 quaerere「寻求」构成「向里寻求」：提问就是搜寻信息。

senses.title: An official investigation
senses.definition: an official process of asking questions to find out the facts about an event
senses.definitionCN: 为查明某一事件真相而进行的正式提问过程
senses.example: A public inquiry was held into the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 就那起事故举行了公开调查。
senses.why: When a whole institution asks the questions, the inquiry becomes an investigation with a verdict at the end.
senses.whyCN: 当一个机构来提问时，inquiry 就成了带结论的调查。

senses.title: Careful study of a question
senses.definition: the act of examining a subject carefully in order to understand it
senses.definitionCN: 为理解某一问题而进行的细致考察
senses.example: Scientific inquiry depends on evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 科学探究依赖证据。
senses.why: The same seeking applies to ideas: to inquire into nature is to look for its causes.
senses.whyCN: 这种「寻求」也适用于思想：探究自然是去找它的成因。

intro.en: Inquiry is a Latin compound meaning to seek into, and it covers both a polite question and a formal probe.
intro.cn: inquiry 是拉丁语意为「向里寻求」的复合词，兼指礼貌的提问与正式调查。

items.en: Quaerere meant "to seek, ask", the source of question, query and quest.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求、询问」，是 question、query、quest 的来源。

items.en: Inquirere, from in- plus quaerere, meant "to seek into, investigate".
items.cn: inquirere 由 in- 加 quaerere 构成，意为「向里寻求、调查」。

items.en: Inquisitio was a legal searching out of facts, the noun behind English inquiry.
items.cn: inquisitio 是法律上对事实的追查，是英语 inquiry 背后的名词。

items.en: Old French enquerre passed the verb to English as enquire and inquire.
items.cn: 古法语 enquerre 把动词传入英语，作 enquire 与 inquire。

items.en: The noun inquiry serves both everyday questions and official investigations.
items.cn: 名词 inquiry 兼用于日常询问与正式调查。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of seeking; the near-meaning group gathers other words for questions and probes.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「寻求」动词；近义组收其他表示提问与调查的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to ask or investigate.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「询问、调查」。

entries.definition: A single sentence that seeks an answer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「问题」，同根。

entries.definition: Eager to know and to ask, often about others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「好问的、好奇的」。

entries.definition: A systematic official search for facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调查」，强调系统、正式地查明事实。

entries.definition: A thorough enquiry, often by journalists or officials.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「探查」，常指记者或官员的深入追查。

entries.definition: The act of politely asking for something to be given.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「请求」，指礼貌地要求某物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use quaerere, the Latin verb of seeking, and the phrases inquiry appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「寻求」动词 quaerere，以及 inquiry 的常用搭配。

normal.en: Quaerere is to seek: an inquiry is a search, with words as the torch.
normal.cn: quaerere 是「寻求」：inquiry 是一次搜寻，言语就是火把。

normal.en: Question and inquiry share the root: one is a single question, the other a search.
normal.cn: question 与 inquiry 同根：前者是单个问题，后者是一次查寻。

normal.en: Make an inquiry is the polite phrase; hold an inquiry is the official one.
normal.cn: make an inquiry 是礼貌说法，hold an inquiry 是官方说法。

normal.en: British spelling often writes enquiry for a simple question.
normal.cn: 英式拼写常用 enquiry 指简单询问。

normal.en: A formal inquiry into the accident lasted a year.
normal.cn: 对这起事故的正式调查持续了一年。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held into a dark room: enquiry is light aimed at what is unknown.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯举进暗室：探究就是照向未知的光。

abstract.en: Every question is a small expedition into someone else's knowledge.
abstract.cn: 每个问题都是进入他人知识领域的一次小型远征。

abstract.en: Good inquiry asks without assuming, and listens without hurrying.
abstract.cn: 好的询问不预设答案，也不急着插话。

examples.en: We have had many inquiries about the job.
examples.cn: 我们收到了许多关于这份工作的询问。

examples.en: An independent inquiry was set up into the fire.
examples.cn: 就这场火灾成立了独立调查。

examples.en: Free inquiry is the basis of any science.
examples.cn: 自由探究是一切科学的基础。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因快瑞」——因想快点知道结果，就去询问调查

root: 拉丁语 quaerere「寻求、询问」加 in-「向内」构成 inquirere「探究」，名词 inquisitio 经古法语 enquere 传入英语，作 inquire 与 inquiry；同根词有 question、query、quest、inquisitive。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses on one thread: a question, an official investigation, and the careful study of a subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项串在一条线上：一个问题、一次正式调查，以及对某一课题的细致探究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp is held into a dark room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯被举进黑暗的房间。

branches.en: THE DESK: many inquiries arrive at an office that serves the public.
branches.cn: 服务台这条线：公共机构会收到大量 inquiry。

branches.en: THE LETTER: a written inquiry asks politely and waits for a reply.
branches.cn: 信件这条线：书面 inquiry 礼貌发问，静待回复。

branches.en: THE COURT: an official inquiry gathers evidence and publishes a report.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：正式 inquiry 收集证据并公布报告。

branches.en: THE LAB: scientific inquiry tests ideas against evidence.
branches.cn: 实验室这条线：科学探究用证据检验观念。

branches.en: THE THREAD: each sense is a structured search for what is not yet known.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都是对未知之物的有组织搜寻。

intro.en: Inquiry is a Latin prefix on a Latin verb of seeking, with a noun ending added.
intro.cn: inquiry 由拉丁语前缀加「寻求」动词构成，再加名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere, inquirere and inquisitio are recorded; the spelling with y is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quaerere、inquirere、inquisitio 均有记录；带 y 的拼写是英语的变化。

The root also gives question.
The compound behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是本词背后的复合动词。

It shapes the English noun.
