由本词换后缀构成，义为「检查员；督察」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「检查性质的」

senses.title: A careful examination
senses.definition: an official or careful look at something in order to find faults or judge quality
senses.definitionCN: 为找出问题或判断质量而进行的正式、仔细的查看
senses.example: The car passed inspection without a single fault.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车通过检查时没有任何故障。
senses.why: Latin specere means to look; inspection is the noun of looking into a thing closely.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 specere 意为「看」；inspection 就是凑近往里面看的那个动作的名词。

senses.title: An official visit to check
senses.definition: an official visit by an authority to check that rules are being followed
senses.definitionCN: 权力机构为核查规则是否被遵守而进行的正式到访
senses.example: The school prepares for inspection every second year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校每隔一年准备迎接视察。
senses.why: The look becomes institutional: someone with authority comes to see whether things are done correctly.
senses.whyCN: 这种「看」被制度化了：有权的人前来看事情是否做得对。

senses.title: The act of looking closely
senses.definition: the act of examining something closely with your own eyes, often to notice details
senses.definitionCN: 用自己的眼睛仔细查看某物，往往是为了发现细节
senses.example: On closer inspection, the painting turned out to be a copy.
senses.exampleCN: 细看之下，那幅画原来是仿作。
senses.why: The oldest and simplest sense: bending down to see what the eye misses at a distance.
senses.whyCN: 最古老、最简单的义项：俯下身去看远处看不见的东西。

intro.en: Inspection is a Latin noun of action from inspicere "to look into", built on specere "to see".
intro.cn: inspection 是拉丁语 inspicere「向里看」的行为名词，基于 specere「看」。

items.en: Specere "to look at" was one of the basic verbs of seeing in Latin.
items.cn: specere「看」是拉丁语中最基本的视觉动词之一。

items.en: In- plus specere gave inspicere, "to look into, examine".
items.cn: in- 加 specere 得到 inspicere，意为「向里看、查察」。

items.en: The noun of action inspectio named the examination itself.
items.cn: 行为名词 inspectio 指查看这件事本身。

items.en: Old French passed inspection into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把 inspection 传入英语。

items.en: Industrial and school inspection gave the word its official, regular sense.
items.cn: 工业检查与学校视察赋予了它官方、定期的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares Latin spec- "look"; the near-meaning group holds other words for examining.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 spec-「看」；近义组收其他表示「检查」的词。

entries.definition: Someone who watches, built on the same looking root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观众」，用同一「看」词根构成。

entries.definition: To think someone is guilty, literally "to look up from below".
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「怀疑」，字面是「从下往上看」。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to look into closely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，是本词背后的动词，义为「仔细查看」。

entries.definition: A close testing look, wider and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审查」，范围更宽、更正式。

entries.definition: A quick test that looks right or works.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「检查」，强调快速确认是否正常。

entries.definition: An official examination of financial records.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计」，指对财务记录的正式检查。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the root spec- "look" and the prepositions that go with the word.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用词根 spec-「看」以及这个词常用的介词搭配。

normal.en: spec- is to look: inspection is looking in.
normal.cn: spec- 是「看」：inspection 就是往里看。

normal.en: Spectator, suspect and inspect all share the root.
normal.cn: spectator、suspect、inspect 共享词根。

normal.en: On inspection, the engine had two loose bolts.
normal.cn: 经检查，发动机上有两颗松动的螺栓。

normal.en: A safety inspection happens before a factory reopens.
normal.cn: 工厂复工前会做安全检查。

normal.en: Close inspection often finds what a quick glance misses.
normal.cn: 细看常能发现一眼扫过所遗漏的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a beam of light moving slowly along a seam.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光沿着接缝慢慢移动。

abstract.en: An inspection is a conversation between the eye and the object.
abstract.cn: 检查是眼睛与物件之间的一场对话。

abstract.en: What survives inspection deserves trust; what avoids it does not.
abstract.cn: 经得起检查的东西值得信任，躲避检查的不值得。

examples.en: The building failed its fire inspection.
examples.cn: 这座建筑未通过消防检查。

examples.en: On inspection, the letter proved to be false.
examples.cn: 经查看，那封信原来是伪造的。

examples.en: Officials made an inspection of the harbour.
examples.cn: 官员们对港口进行了视察。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯佩克」——按品牌要求一项项查看，就是检查

root: 拉丁语 specere「看」→ in- + specere = inspicere「向里看、查察」→ 行为名词 inspectio「检查」→ 古法语 → 十四世纪英语 inspection。spec-/spect- 也见于 spectacle、spectator、suspect、respect。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a careful examination, an official visit, and plain close looking.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：仔细检查、官方视察，以及朴素的「细看」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gloved hand guides a torch along a weld, inch by inch.
core.cn: 核心意象：戴手套的手拿着手电沿着焊縫一寸寸照。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: a machine is checked for faults.
branches.cn: 车间这条线：检查机器有无故障。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: an authority visits to enforce rules.
branches.cn: 机关这条线：权力部门到访核查规则。

branches.en: THE GALLERY: a closer look changes what we think.
branches.cn: 画廊这条线：凑近细看改变了我们的判断。

branches.en: THE LINK: official and personal inspection both rest on looking closely.
branches.cn: 连接线：官方检查与个人细看都靠凑近看。

branches.en: THE SCHEDULE: the official sense is regular and predictable.
branches.cn: 日程线：官方义是定期、可预期的。

intro.en: Inspection is in- "into" plus spec- "look", with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: inspection 是 in-「向内」加 spec-「看」，再加名词词尾 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere, inspicere and inspectio are attested, so no reconstruction is needed for this layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere、inspicere、inspectio 均有记载，这一层无需重构。

items.example: It directs the looking inward.
The root runs through spectacles and spectator.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根贯穿 spectacles 与 spectator。

items.example: The compound is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这一复合动词是直接来源。

items.example: It makes an abstract noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 它构成抽象的行为名词。

items.example: Inspector names the person who checks.
The same root with a different prefix-free form.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根的无前缀形式。

items.example: Re- gives the sense of looking back.
Sub- "under" plus the same root.

definition_en: to give someone the desire or confidence to do something, or to be the cause of an idea
core_image: 一口气吹进原本微弱的小火苗，火焰一下窜高起来
scene: 音乐教室里几个学生低着头，不敢开口。Her first teacher inspired her to become a writer.
sceneCN: 这里 inspire 是「激励、鼓舞」（第 1 个义项：使人产生做某事的愿望或信心），句意是她第一位老师激励她成为作家。画面里可想象的物件：钢琴、谱架、向外窜起的火苗。

pos.zh: 动词：鼓舞；激励；启发；激起

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「灵感；鼓舞」
由现在分词构成，义为「鼓舞人心的」
由过去分词构成，义为「受到启发的」
由 inspiration 加 -al 构成，义为「鼓舞人心的」

senses.title: To give an urge or confidence
senses.definition: to give someone the wish, courage, or energy to do something important
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做重要之事的愿望、勇气或力量
senses.example: The coach inspired the team to play beyond their level.
senses.exampleCN: 教练激励球队打出超常的水平。
senses.why: Latin spirare means to breathe; in- adds "in", so to inspire is literally to breathe courage into someone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 spirare 意为「呼吸」；in- 加「向内」，所以 inspire 字面上是「把勇气吹进某人」。

senses.title: To be the cause of an idea
senses.definition: to make someone have a new idea or create something, often without intending to
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生新想法或创作出作品，往往并非有意为之
senses.example: The old harbour inspired her best paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老港口激发了她最好的画作。
senses.why: The breath enters from outside: a place or a person fills the mind with an idea.
senses.whyCN: 「气」从外面吹进来：一个地方或一个人让头脑里充满了想法。

senses.title: To cause a feeling
senses.definition: to produce a strong feeling such as trust, fear, or respect in other people
senses.definitionCN: 在他人心中产生信任、恐惧或尊敬等强烈情绪
senses.example: His calm voice inspired confidence in the passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 他沉稳的声音让乘客产生了信心。
senses.why: Feelings are breathed into people too, so the same verb covers courage, awe and confidence.
senses.whyCN: 情绪同样是被「吹进」人心的，所以同一动词也覆盖勇气、敬畏与信心。

intro.en: Inspire comes from Latin inspirare "to breathe in", a verb that became especially common in religious writing.
intro.cn: inspire 来自拉丁语 inspirare「吹气进去、呼吸」，这个动词在宗教文献中尤其常见。

items.en: Spirare "to breathe" is the root behind spirit, soul and breath words.
items.cn: spirare「呼吸」是 spirit、soul 等「气息」类词的词根。

items.en: Inspirare meant both to breathe in and to blow into something.
items.cn: inspirare 既指吸气，也指把气吹进某物。

items.en: In Christian Latin it described god breathing spirit into a person.
items.cn: 基督教拉丁语用它描述神把灵吹入人身。

items.en: Old French inspirer brought the verb into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 inspirer 把这一动词带入中古英语。

items.en: The modern sense of encouraging or stimulating an idea grows in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 现代「激励、启发」义在十七世纪发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares Latin spir- "breathe"; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of encouragement.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 spir-「呼吸」；近义组收其他表示「鼓励」的动词。

entries.definition: The breath of life or a mood, from the same breathing root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「精神、情绪」，词根同为「呼吸」。

entries.definition: To breathe, with the prefix re- meaning back or again.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「呼吸」，前缀 re- 表「回、再」。

entries.definition: To come to an end, literally to breathe out for the last time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「到期、死亡」，字面是「呼出最后一口气」。

entries.definition: To give someone courage, plainer than inspire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「鼓励」，比 inspire 朴素直白。

entries.definition: To give a reason for acting, often in a practical context.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激发动机」，多用于实际情境。

entries.definition: To rouse interest or activity, especially thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「刺激、激发」，多指激发兴趣或思考。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the breathing root spir- and the prepositions inspire takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「呼吸」词根 spir- 以及 inspire 所带的介词。

normal.en: spir- is breath: to inspire is to breathe in courage.
normal.cn: spir- 是呼吸：inspire 就是吸入勇气。

normal.en: Spirit, respire and expire all come from breathing.
normal.cn: spirit、respire、expire 都源于「呼吸」。

normal.en: Be inspired by someone, and inspire someone to act.
normal.cn: 受某人启发，也去激励别人行动。

normal.en: Leaders inspire confidence even when the news is bad.
normal.cn: 坏消息来了，领导者仍能激发信心。

normal.en: An inspiring talk changes what the audience does next week.
normal.cn: 鼓舞人心的演讲改变了听众下周的行动。

abstract.en: Picture a slow breath blown onto a dying ember.
abstract.cn: 想象一口慢气吹在将熄的炭火上。

abstract.en: Inspiration arrives from outside the mind, like air.
abstract.cn: 灵感像空气一样从头脑之外进来。

abstract.en: People remember who breathed courage into them.
abstract.cn: 人总记得是谁给自己吹入过勇气。

examples.en: Her calm manner inspired trust among the patients.
examples.cn: 她沉静的态度让病人产生了信任。

examples.en: The mountain village inspired several of his novels.
examples.cn: 那个山村激发了他好几部小说的灵感。

examples.en: The coach inspired the young players to keep trying.
examples.cn: 教练激励年轻球员继续努力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬死派」——鼓起勇气硬要派出去，就是被激励了

root: 拉丁语 spirare「呼吸、吹气」→ in- + spirare = inspirare「吸气；吹气进去」→ 基督教拉丁语指神把灵吹入人身 → 古法语 inspirer → 中古英语。spir- 也见于 spirit、respire、expire、conspire。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: breathing courage into people, filling minds with ideas, and raising a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：把勇气吹进人心、让头脑充满想法，以及激起某种情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a breath is blown onto a weak flame and it rises.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口气吹向微弱的火苗，火焰窜高。

branches.en: THE COACH: courage is given, and action follows.
branches.cn: 教练这条线：勇气被给予，行动随之而来。

branches.en: THE STUDIO: a place fills the mind with ideas.
branches.cn: 画室这条线：一个地方让头脑充满想法。

branches.en: THE HALL: a voice raises confidence or awe.
branches.cn: 大厅这条线：声音引起信心或敬畏。

branches.en: THE LINK: the feeling is always breathed in from someone else.
branches.cn: 连接线：情绪总是从别人那里被吹入。

branches.en: THE TONE: the idea sense is quieter and less active.
branches.cn: 语气线：「启发」义更安静、更不主动。

intro.en: Inspire is in- "into" plus the Latin breathing root spir-, with a French verb ending.
intro.cn: inspire 是 in-「向内」加拉丁「呼吸」词根 spir-，再带法语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare, inspirare and the noun inspiratio are all recorded in classical and Christian texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spirare、inspirare 及名词 inspiratio 在古典与基督教文献中均有记载。

items.example: It marks the breath going in.
The root appears in spirit and expire.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根见于 spirit 与 expire。

items.example: The compound is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这一复合动词是直接来源。

items.example: Inspiration names the effect.
items.exampleCN: Inspiration 指这种作用的结果。

items.example: Inspiring describes a person or event.
The root survives directly.
Re- adds the idea of return.
Con- means together.

definition_en: to put equipment or software in place ready for use, or to put someone formally into an office
core_image: 两个人在墙上量好位置，把一台新机器固定牢，插上电
scene: 梯子靠在墙边，工具箱摊开在地板上。The engineers will install the new heating system before winter.
sceneCN: 这里 install 是「安装」（第 1 个义项：把设备或软件安置好以便使用），句意是工程师会在入冬前安装新的供暖系统。画面里能看到的物件：梯子、工具箱、机器、电线。

pos.zh: 动词：安装；设置；正式任命

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「安装；装置」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「安装者；安装程序」
由本词与 art 构成的复合名词，义为「装置艺术」

senses.title: To put equipment in place
senses.definition: to fix a machine, device, or piece of equipment in position and connect it so that it works
senses.definitionCN: 把机器、装置或设备固定在位置上并接好线，使其能工作
senses.example: They installed a shower in the small bathroom.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在小浴室里装了淋浴。
senses.why: Latin in- "in" plus stallum "a place, a stall": to install is to set something in its proper place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in-「入」加 stallum「位置、座位」：install 就是把东西放到它该在的位置上。

senses.title: To set up software
senses.definition: to copy a program onto a computer or phone and prepare it to run
senses.definitionCN: 把程序复制到电脑或手机上并准备好运行
senses.example: It took ten minutes to install the app.
senses.exampleCN: 装这个应用花了十分钟。
senses.why: The medieval seat became a digital one: the program is put into place inside the machine.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的「座位」变成了数字的：程序被放进机器的位置里。

senses.title: To put someone into an office
senses.definition: to place a person formally in an official position, often with a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 以仪式等方式正式把某人安置到官职上
senses.example: The new bishop was installed in the cathedral in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 新主教春天在大教堂正式就职。
senses.why: The oldest sense: a person is seated in a stall, the literal seat of office.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项：人坐进 stallum（座位），即「入座就职」。

intro.en: Install comes from medieval Latin installare "to place in a stall or seat", a church word first.
intro.cn: install 来自中世纪拉丁语 installare「安置到座位里」，最初是教会用语。

items.en: Stallum meant a standing place, a stall, or a seat in a choir.
items.cn: stallum 指站立之处、摊位，或唱诗班的座位。

items.en: Installare "to put into a stall" was used of clergy placed in a prebend or a canonry.
items.cn: installare「放入座位」用于指把教士安置到俸禄或教会职位上。

items.en: Old French installer carried the word into secular use for any placing in office.
items.cn: 古法语 installer 使这个词进入世俗用法，泛指就职。

items.en: English borrowed the verb with the sense "to place" from the fifteenth century, first for church appointments.
items.cn: 英语从十五世纪起用其「安放」之义，最初用于教会任命。

items.en: Industrial and computing usage later extended it to machines and software.
items.cn: 后来的工业与计算机用法又把它扩展到机器与软件。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -stall place word; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of putting things in place.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -stall「位置」这一部分；近义组收其他表示「放置」的动词。

entries.definition: A booth or a stable compartment, the literal place of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「摊位、隔间」，是词根字面的「位置」。

entries.definition: The act of installing, or the equipment installed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「安装」或「装好的装置」。

entries.definition: A person or program that installs something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「安装者」或「安装程序」。

entries.definition: To put a part in place and make it work, common in British speech.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装配」，英式口语常用。

entries.definition: To prepare equipment for use, often on a temporary basis.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「设置」，常指临时搭建。

entries.definition: To fix something firmly onto a surface or frame.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「镶嵌、安装」，强调牢固固定在表面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal "seat" inside the word and the objects people install.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用词内字面的「座位」，以及人们真实安装的东西。

normal.en: in plus stall: put the thing into its stall.
normal.cn: in 加 stall：把东西放进它的位置。

normal.en: Stall is still a booth; install is seating a machine.
normal.cn: stall 仍是摊位；install 是让机器落座。

normal.en: Install software, then install the printer.
normal.cn: 先装软件，再装打印机。

normal.en: A bishop is installed in a cathedral seat.
normal.cn: 主教的就职是在教堂的座位上完成的。

normal.en: Two l is correct: installed, not installd.
normal.cn: 过去式要双写 l：installed。

abstract.en: Every installation is a promise that the thing will stay put.
abstract.cn: 每一次安装都是一份「它会留着不动」的承诺。

abstract.en: A new habit must be installed like a new boiler.
abstract.cn: 新习惯要像新锅炉一样被装进去。

abstract.en: Installing is a small ceremony of order.
abstract.cn: 安装是一场微小的秩序仪式。

examples.en: We installed new locks on every door.
examples.cn: 我们在每扇门上都装了新锁。

examples.en: The software installs itself in a few minutes.
examples.cn: 这个软件几分钟就自动装好了。

examples.en: He was installed as head of the department last year.
examples.cn: 他去年正式就任部门负责人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬装」——硬要装进去，就是安装

root: 中世纪拉丁语 stallum「站立处、摊位、座位」→ installare「放入座位」→ 古法语 installer → 十五世纪英语。最早用于教会就职，后转指机器与软件的安装。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: fixing equipment, copying software, and seating a person in office.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：固定设备、装软件，以及让人正式就职。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two workers measure the wall and bolt a new machine firmly in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个工人量好墙面，把新机器牢牢固定住。

branches.en: THE WALL: a boiler or camera is fixed and connected.
branches.cn: 墙面这条线：锅炉或摄像头被固定并接线。

branches.en: THE SCREEN: a program is put in its place inside the machine.
branches.cn: 屏幕这条线：程序被放进机器的位置里。

branches.en: THE CATHEDRAL: a person is seated in the stall of office.
branches.cn: 教堂这条线：人被安置到官职的座位上。

branches.en: THE LINK: physical and digital installation share the idea of a proper place.
branches.cn: 连接线：实体与数字安装共享「恰当位置」的观念。

branches.en: THE ROOT: the office sense is the oldest, and the others are echoes of it.
branches.cn: 根源线：就职义最古老，其余义项是它的回声。

intro.en: Install is in- "into" plus the medieval Latin stallum "a place, stall", as a verb installare.
intro.cn: install 是 in-「入」加中世纪拉丁语 stallum「位置、摊位」构成的动词 installare。

latinIntro.en: Stallum and installare are recorded in medieval Latin; the deeper Germanic origin of stallum is not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: stallum 与 installare 有中世纪拉丁语记载，但 stallum 更深的日耳曼来源不属于拉丁语。

items.example: It marks putting into a place.
The noun supplies the destination.
The verb is the direct source.
Installation names the act.
Installer names the person or program.
The bare noun survives in English.
items.exampleCN: 不带前缀的名词仍在英语中使用。

items.example: A different word from the same family.
British usage sometimes drops one l.
items.exampleCN: 英式有时只写一个 l。

definition_zh: 分期付款；一期；一集；部分
definition_en: one of several regular payments for a debt; one part of a series
core_image: 一本日历，每个月都被划掉一个方格，方格上标着小小的金额数字
scene: 小丽想买一台最新款的电脑，商店说可以分十期付，每期两百块。She decided the installment plan was easier than paying all at once.
sceneCN: 这里 installment 指「分期付款的一期」（第 1 个义项：债务的定期分期付款之一）；句意为他们选择分月付而不是一次性付清。图中可辨识物件：日历、电脑、分期付款收据。

pos.zh: 分期付款（可数）；一集（可数）

derivatives.zh: 安装；设立
安装；设施
安装人员
分期付款方案
装置艺术

senses.title: regular debt payment
senses.definition: one of a series of scheduled payments to settle a debt
senses.definitionCN: 结清债务的一系列预定付款之一
senses.example: The loan required twelve monthly instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔贷款要求分十二个月偿还。
senses.why: The root is install, 'to set up', as in setting up a schedule of payments.
senses.whyCN: 词根是 install「设立」，就像设立一个付款日程。

senses.title: part of a purchase
senses.definition: one part of the price of an item paid over time
senses.definitionCN: 一件商品的价格中按时间分批支付的一部分
senses.example: They bought the fridge on easy instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以轻松分期的方式买下了冰箱。
senses.why: A purchase that you set up with a payment plan.
senses.whyCN: 通过付款计划设立的一笔消费。

senses.title: episode of a story
senses.definition: one episode of a serial story, television show or podcast
senses.definitionCN: 连载故事、电视剧或播客的一集
senses.example: The novel was published in monthly instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说按月连载。
senses.why: A story set up to come out piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 被设立成一段一段推出的故事。

senses.title: stage of a plan
senses.definition: one stage of an overall plan or project
senses.definitionCN: 整体计划或项目的一个阶段
senses.example: The first instalment of the highway opened in 2024.
senses.exampleCN: 高速公路的一期在 2024 年通车。
senses.why: A large work set up as a series of smaller bits.
senses.whyCN: 一项大工程被设立成若干小块。

senses.title: artwork installation
senses.definition: a large artwork set up in a specific space
senses.definitionCN: 设立在特定空间里的大型艺术作品
senses.example: The museum commissioned a new instalment.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆委托创作了一件新的装置作品。
senses.why: A work that is installed, set up in a space.
senses.whyCN: 一件被 install、设立在空间里的作品。

senses.title: initial payment
senses.definition: the first payment in a series
senses.definitionCN: 一系列付款中的第一笔
senses.example: The first instalment was due on delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 首期款在交货时到期。
senses.why: The first of the scheduled pieces.
senses.whyCN: 预定的几块中的第一块。

senses.title: supplement or tranche
senses.definition: a supplementary sum of money released over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间分批释放的一笔追加资金
senses.example: The donor promised a second instalment in 2026.
senses.exampleCN: 捐赠者承诺 2026 年捐出第二期款项。
senses.why: Money set up to come in slices.
senses.whyCN: 被设立成一片片进来的钱。

senses.title: scheduled meeting
senses.definition: a scheduled session of a course or training programme
senses.definitionCN: 课程或培训项目预定的一节课
senses.example: The leadership course had six fortnightly instalments.
senses.exampleCN: 这个领导力课程分六次，每两周一次。
senses.why: A course set up as pieces over time.
senses.whyCN: 一门被设立成若干块、按时间推出的课程。

intro.en: Instalment comes from install 'to set up, arrange' + -ment. Install itself came from Old French installer, from Latin installare.
intro.cn: instalment 来自 install「设立、安排」+ -ment。install 本身来自古法语 installer，后者来自拉丁语 installare。

items.en: Latin installare meant 'to place in a seat, to install in an office'; it was in- 'in' + stallum 'seat, stall'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 installare 意为「安置在座位上、任命」，由 in-「在……里」+ stallum「座位、栏」构成。

items.en: Old French installer meant 'to install, establish'.
items.cn: 古法语 installer 意为「安装、设立」。

items.en: English install was borrowed around 1400 meaning 'to place formally, to establish'.
items.cn: 英语 install 约 1400 年从古法语借入，意为「正式安置、设立」。

items.en: Instalment was formed from install + -ment around 1560, first meaning 'an arrangement, a setting up'.
items.cn: instalment 约 1560 年由 install + -ment 构成，最初意为「一个安排、一次设立」。

items.en: The 'partial payment' sense developed from the idea of 'setting up a debt to be paid in parts', by the 18th century.
items.cn: 「分期付款」义来自「设立一笔要分几块还的债」的想法，18 世纪形成。

items.en: Installment (US) and instalment (UK) are both standard; the Latin root stallum is well attested.
items.cn: 美式 installment 和英式 instalment 都是标准拼写；拉丁词根 stallum 来源可靠。

note.en: Look-alikes share the install root; near meanings are one of several payments or parts.
note.cn: 形近共享 install 词根；近义是若干付款或部分中的一个。

entries.definition: To set up or place; instalment is the noun of a piece of what is set up.
entries.definitionCN: 设立、安置；instalment 是被设立的东西的一块。

entries.definition: The act of installing, or a facility set up.
entries.definitionCN: 安装行为，或设立的设施。

entries.definition: A person who installs something.
entries.definitionCN: 安装工。

entries.definition: A seat or enclosure, from the Latin stallum.
entries.definitionCN: 座位或栏，来自拉丁语 stallum。

entries.definition: Any amount paid, not necessarily part of a scheduled series.
entries.definitionCN: 任何支付的金额，不一定是预定系列中的一部分。

entries.definition: One scheduled piece of a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 更大整体中预定好的一块。

entries.definition: A slice of money released over time; usually financial.
entries.definitionCN: 按时间分批释放的一笔资金块；通常指财务。

entries.definition: One part of a serial story, same as the story sense of instalment.
entries.definitionCN: 连载故事的一部分，跟 instalment 的故事义相同。

normalIntro.en: Real morphemes and real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实复合。

normal.en: install 'to set up' + -ment = a piece of what has been set up (schedule, series, debt).
normal.cn: install「设立」+ -ment = 被设立的东西（日程、系列、债务）中的一块。

normal.en: stallum is Latin for 'seat, stall'; installare means 'to place in a seat'.
normal.cn: stallum 拉丁语意为「座位、栏」；installare 意为「安置在座位上」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: monthly instalment, pay in instalments, instalment plan.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：monthly instalment 月供、pay in instalments 分期付、instalment plan 分期方案。

normal.en: install, installation, instalment are a tidy family.
normal.cn: install、installation、instalment 是整齐的同族。

normal.en: US uses -ll-: installment; UK uses -l-: instalment.
normal.cn: 美式双 l 拼 installment，英式单 l 拼 instalment。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with bricks being laid one by one, each brick an instalment.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙一块块砌起来，每一块砖就是一期。

abstract.en: Picture a judge installing a judge on the bench, then the bench splits into twelve pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法官坐在宝座上，然后宝座分裂成十二块。

abstract.en: Picture each month a piece of your debt falls off.
abstract.cn: 想象每个月你的债务就掉下一块。

examples.en: She chose an interest-free instalment plan to buy her first camera.
examples.cn: 她选择了免息分期方案买下了自己的第一台相机。

examples.en: The author released the novel in weekly instalments through an online platform.
examples.cn: 作者通过网络平台把这部小说按周连载。

examples.en: Only after the final instalment was paid did the title to the car transfer to her.
examples.cn: 只有在最后一期付清后，汽车的所有权才转移到她名下。

dict_mnemonic.text: install（设立）+ -ment = 被设立的一件事被拆成几块 → 分期

root: 拉丁语 installare（in-「在……里」+ stallum「座位、栏」）→ 古法语 installer → 英语 install + -ment → instalment。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses progress from scheduled debt payment → part of a purchase → story episode → project stage → artwork → initial payment → supplementary funds → course session.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从预定债务付款 → 购买款的一部分 → 故事一集 → 项目阶段 → 装置艺术 → 首期 → 追加资金 → 课程一节课。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar where each month you place one small coin on the debt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本日历，每个月你都往债务上放一枚小硬币。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL SLICE: one part of a payment plan for debt or purchase.
branches.cn: 财务上的一块：债务或购买款付款计划中的一部分。

branches.en: THE STORY SLICE: one episode of a serial work.
branches.cn: 故事上的一块：连载作品的一集。

branches.en: THE CONSTRUCTION SLICE: a project stage or an artwork installation.
branches.cn: 工程上的一块：项目阶段或装置艺术。

branches.en: THE FUND SLICE: the first or a supplementary tranche.
branches.cn: 资金上的一块：首期或追加的一笔。

branches.en: THE EDUCATIONAL SLICE: one scheduled session of a course.
branches.cn: 教育上的一块：课程的一节预定课。

intro.en: Installment = install + -ment. Install ← French installer ← Latin installare.
intro.cn: installment = install + -ment。install ← 法 installer ← 拉丁 installare。

latinIntro.en: Latin installare = in- + stallum. stallum = seat, stall.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 installare = in- + stallum。stallum = 座位、栏。

items.example: You install a schedule of payments.

items.meaning: a piece of what is installed
items.example: Each payment is one instalment of the schedule.
items.exampleCN: 每一次付款就是日程里的一期。

items.example: The root is a physical seat or stall.
items.exampleCN: 词根是一个物理的座位或栏。

items.example: in- puts you into the stallum.

items.structure: Old English steall, related to Latin stallum
items.meaning: a seat, a booth, or to be stuck
items.example: Stall shares a root with Latin stallum.
items.exampleCN: stall 与拉丁语 stallum 同根。

items.meaning: the act of installing or a facility
items.example: A power station is an installation.
The installer came to fit the new dishwasher.
Instalment is the result of install + -ment.
items.exampleCN: Instalment 是 install + -ment 的结果。

items.example: Installation uses the different suffix -ation.
items.exampleCN: Installation 用的是另一个后缀 -ation。

items.example: Reinstall the software if it stalls.
items.exampleCN: 如果软件卡住了就重装。

latinEntries.meaning: to place in a seat; to install

definition_en: a natural ability or urge to behave in a certain way without being taught
core_image: 雏鸟在蛋壳刚裂开时，就朝着光的方向伸出脖子
scene: 海边沙滩上，刚出壳的小龟没有谁教，直接朝海浪爬去。Birds find their way home by instinct, not by memory.
sceneCN: 这里 instinct 是「本能」（第 1 个义项：无需学习的天生行为能力或倾向），句意是鸟靠本能而非记忆找到回家的路。画面里能看到的物件：蛋壳、沙滩、海浪、光。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「本能的；直觉的」
由 instinctive 加 -ly 构成，义为「本能地」
由本词加 -ual 构成，义为「本能的」，多用于心理 学

senses.title: A natural urge
senses.definition: a natural tendency to act in a particular way, present from birth and not learned
senses.definitionCN: 从出生起就有、并非学来的行为倾向
senses.example: A cat has an instinct to hide its waste.
senses.exampleCN: 猫有掩埋粪便的本能。
senses.why: Latin instinctus was an inner impulse; the word kept that image of something urging from inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instinctus 指内在冲动；这个词保留了「体内有东西在催促」的意象。

senses.title: A gut feeling
senses.definition: a feeling about what is right or dangerous, felt before any reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 在推理之前就对对错或危险产生的感觉
senses.example: My instinct told me not to sign the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 我的直觉告诉我不要签这份文件。
senses.why: The inner urge is felt as knowledge: the same push now warns rather than drives.
senses.whyCN: 内在的驱使被感受为一种认识：同一股推力如今是在警告，而不是在驱动。

senses.title: A natural talent
senses.definition: a natural ability for something that seems to come without training
senses.definitionCN: 看似无需训练就有的能力
senses.example: She has an instinct for finding good stories.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生善于发现好故事。
senses.why: When the natural push meets a kind of work, it looks like talent rather than urge.
senses.whyCN: 当这股天生的推力遇上某类工作时，它看起来像天赋而不像冲动。

intro.en: Instinct is a Latin noun from instinguere "to prick or urge on", pictured as an inner goad.
intro.cn: instinct 来自拉丁语 instinguere「刺、驱使」的名词形式，意象是体内有一根刺在催动。

items.en: Stinguere meant to prick or goad, related to the mark or point of a sting.
items.cn: stinguere 意为「刺、驱使」，与刺点、刺痕有关。

items.en: In- plus stinguere gave instinguere, "to urge on from within".
items.cn: in- 加 stinguere 得到 instinguere，意为「从内部驱使」。

items.en: The noun instinctus meant an impulse or inspiration.
items.cn: 名词 instinctus 意为「冲动、灵感」。

items.en: In the seventeenth century it was applied to the behaviour of animals.
items.cn: 十七世纪起用于描述动物的行为。

items.en: Psychology later extended it to human urges and untaught reactions.
items.cn: 后来的心理学把它扩展到人的冲动与未经学习的反应。

note.en: The look-alike group looks and sounds like instinct; the near-meaning group holds other words for untaught knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组在外形和读音上接近 instinct；近义组收其他表示「未学而知」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning done without thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「本能的」，指不经思考就做。

entries.definition: Clearly separate; the same looking ending, a different Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「截然不同的」，词尾相似但拉丁动词不同。

entries.definition: No longer existing, literally "stung out".
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「灭绝的」，字面是「被熄灭的」。

entries.definition: Knowledge felt without reasons, close to gut feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「直觉」，指没有理由的感觉。

entries.definition: A sudden wish to act, often short-lived.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冲动」，常是短暂的。

entries.definition: An automatic bodily reaction, narrower than instinct.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「反射」，范围比 instinct 窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the image of an inner goad and the phrase by instinct.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「体内有刺在催」的意象，以及短语 by instinct。

normal.en: in plus sting: an instinct is a sting inside that makes you act.
normal.cn: in 加 sting：instinct 就是体内的一根刺，催你行动。

normal.en: Act by instinct; learn by practice.
normal.cn: 本能让你行动，练习让你学会。

normal.en: Trust your instincts when there is no time to think.
normal.cn: 没时间思考时就相信直觉。

normal.en: Instinct is not the same as memory.
normal.cn: 本能不等于记忆。

normal.en: Instinctive is the adjective; instinctively is the adverb.
normal.cn: instinctive 是形容词，instinctively 是副词。

abstract.en: A newborn turtle runs to the sea with nobody teaching it.
abstract.cn: 刚出生的小龟无人教就爬向大海。

abstract.en: Instinct is wisdom stored in the body before the mind.
abstract.cn: 本能是心灵之前就存进身体的智慧。

abstract.en: Reason can explain what instinct decided first.
abstract.cn: 理性只能解释本能先做出的决定。

examples.en: He dived into the water by instinct.
examples.cn: 他本能地跳进水里。

examples.en: Her instinct was to say nothing.
examples.cn: 她的直觉是保持沉默。

examples.en: Birds follow the instinct to fly south in autumn.
examples.cn: 秋天鸟儿依照本能南飞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯汀克」——因为身上像被刺了一下，就本能地躲开

root: 拉丁语 stinguere「刺、点燃」→ in- + stinguere = instinguere「从内部驱使」→ 名词 instinctus「冲动、灵感」→ 十六世纪英语；十七世纪起用于动物行为，后扩展至人的直觉。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a natural urge, a gut feeling, and an untaught talent.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：天生冲动、直觉感觉，以及未经训练的天赋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newly hatched bird stretches towards the light before it can walk.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚出壳的雏鸟还不会走，就朝光伸出脖子。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: behaviour that arrives with birth.
branches.cn: 动物这条线：与生俱来的行为。

branches.en: THE MOMENT OF CHOICE: a feeling before reasoning.
branches.cn: 抉择这条线：推理之前的感觉。

branches.en: THE STORYTELLER: a natural knack for a kind of work.
branches.cn: 讲故事的人这条线：某一类工作的天然本领。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are untaught and quick, one about action and one about judgement.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都未经教导且迅速，一个关乎行动，一个关乎判断。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: the talent sense is looser and more social.
branches.cn: 扩展线：「天赋」义更宽松、更社会性。

intro.en: Instinct is in- "in" plus the Latin root stingu- "prick", with the noun form of the participle.
intro.cn: instinct 是 in-「在内」加拉丁词根 stingu-「刺」，采用分词式的名词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin instinguere and instinctus are attested; the deeper origin of stinguere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instinguere 与 instinctus 均有记载，stinguere 的更早来源并不确定。

items.example: It places the goad inside the creature.
items.exampleCN: 它把这根刺放在生物体内。

items.example: The root also appears in extinct.
The verb is the direct source.
It gives the noun its compact form.
Instinctive means driven by instinct.
items.exampleCN: instinctive 意为受本能驱动的。

items.example: Instinctual is the psychological adjective.
Ex- means out.
Dis- means apart.

definition_en: an organisation set up for research or teaching, or to set such a thing up
core_image: 几个人在空地上立起一块牌子，牌子围出一块新划定的地方
scene: 街角老楼前挂上了一块新铜牌，门厅里刚摆好桌椅。The city decided to institute a new system for waste collection.
sceneCN: 这里 institute 是动词「设立、建立」（第 2 个义项：把制度或机构建立起来），句意是市政府决定设立新的垃圾收集制度。画面里能看到的物件：铜牌、桌椅、牌子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「机构；制度」
由 institution 加 -al 构成，义为「机构的；制度性的」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「已设立的」

senses.title: To set up a rule or system
senses.definition: to start a new rule, system, or practice and put it into effect
senses.definitionCN: 开始实行新的规则、制度或做法
senses.example: The council instituted a fine for late payment.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会设立了逾期缴费罚款。
senses.why: Latin instituere means to set up; a rule is set up much as a building is.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instituere 意为「设立」；规则被设立起来，就像建筑被立起来一样。

senses.title: An organisation for research
senses.definition: a body or building established for research, teaching, or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 为研究、教学或某种专业而建立的机构或场所
senses.example: She works at a small institute studying coastal life.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家研究海岸生物的小研究所工作。
senses.why: The thing set up became the institution itself: first a purpose, then the body that serves it.
senses.whyCN: 被设立起来的东西变成了机构本身：先有一个目的，再有服务于它的组织。

senses.title: To begin a legal action
senses.definition: to start legal proceedings against someone, in formal usage
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法中，对某人提起诉讼
senses.example: The company instituted proceedings against the supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 公司对供应商提起了诉讼。
senses.why: A case is formally set up before a court, so the same verb covers starting it.
senses.whyCN: 案件在法庭上被正式设立起来，所以同一动词也指「提起诉讼」。

intro.en: Institute comes from Latin instituere "to set up, place in position", built on statuere "to make stand".
intro.cn: institute 来自拉丁语 instituere「设立、安置」，基于 statuere「使之站立」。

items.en: Stare "to stand" and its causative statuere "to make stand, set up" are classical.
items.cn: stare「站立」及其使役形式 statuere「使站立、设立」都见于古典拉丁语。

items.en: In- plus statuere gave instituere, "to set up, undertake, teach".
items.cn: in- 加 statuere 得到 instituere，意为「设立、着手、教导」。

items.en: The noun institutum meant a purpose, a custom, or an arrangement.
items.cn: 名词 institutum 意为「目的、惯例、安排」。

items.en: Old French institut carried the noun into English as a name for a learned society.
items.cn: 古法语 institut 把名词传入英语，指学术团体。

items.en: From the eighteenth century institute names technical and research bodies.
items.cn: 自十八世纪起，institute 被用来命名技术与研究机构。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the standing root and the -stitut- stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for founding and organisations.
note.cn: 形近组共享「站立」词根与 -stitut- 词干；近义组收其他表示「设立」与「机构」的词。

entries.definition: An established organisation or custom, the noun of result.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机构、制度」，是结果名词。

entries.definition: To make up or form something, with con- meaning together.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「构成」，前缀 con- 表「共同」。

entries.definition: To put one thing in place of another, with sub- meaning under.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「替换」，前缀 sub- 表「在下」。

entries.definition: To set something up permanently, plainer than institute.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建立」，比 institute 更朴素。

entries.definition: To be the first to start an organisation or city.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「创建」，指最先发起组织或城市。

entries.definition: A learned society or school, a near synonym for the noun sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「研究院、学院」，与名词义近义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the standing root and the double life of the word as noun and verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「站立」词根，以及这个词名词、动词两用的特点。

normal.en: in plus statuere: to set something standing, hence to set up.
normal.cn: in 加 statuere：让某物立起来，故为「设立」。

normal.en: Institute is both the act and the building.
normal.cn: institute 既是动作，也是建筑。

normal.en: A research institute institutes its own rules.
normal.cn: 研究所会设立自己的规矩。

normal.en: Same family as constitute and substitute.
normal.cn: 与 constitute、substitute 同族。

normal.en: The noun stress is on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 名词重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: Picture a sign being planted in empty ground.
abstract.cn: 想象在空地上立起一块牌子。

abstract.en: To institute is to give a habit a fixed address.
abstract.cn: 设立就是给一种习惯一个固定地址。

abstract.en: Institutions outlive the people who institute them.
abstract.cn: 机构比设立它的人活得更久。

examples.en: The school instituted a ban on phones in class.
examples.cn: 学校设立了课堂禁用手机的规定。

examples.en: He joined a research institute after graduation.
examples.cn: 毕业后他进入一家研究所。

examples.en: They instituted a new training programme.
examples.cn: 他们设立了一个新的培训项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬是提土」——硬是提土来立招牌，就是设立机构

root: 拉丁语 stare「站立」→ statuere「使站立、设立」→ in- + statuere = instituere「设立、着手」→ institutum「惯例、安排」→ 古法语 institut → 英语 institute。与 institution、constitute、substitute 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: setting up a rule, the research body itself, and starting legal action.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：设立规则、研究机构本身，以及提起诉讼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sign is planted in empty ground and marks out a new place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块牌子被插进空地，划出一片新领域。

branches.en: THE NOTICE: a new rule is put in force.
branches.cn: 公告这条线：新规则被实行。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: a body created for research or teaching.
branches.cn: 建筑这条线：为研究或教学建立的机构。

branches.en: THE COURT: a case is formally begun.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：正式启动案件。

branches.en: THE LINK: every institute is itself instituted before it institutes anything.
branches.cn: 连接线：任何机构都要先被设立，才能设立别的。

branches.en: THE FORM: the legal sense belongs to a formal register.
branches.cn: 语域线：法律义属于正式语域。

intro.en: Institute is in- "in" plus the Latin statu- "set standing", with a participle ending.
intro.cn: institute 是 in-「入」加拉丁词干 statu-「使站立」，再带分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin statuere, instituere and institutum are all recorded in classical and later texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 statuere、instituere、institutum 在古典及后世文献中均有记载。

definition_en: a large organisation such as a university or hospital, or an established custom
core_image: 石阶、石柱和一扇旧木门，门上的铜牌刻着机构的名字
scene: 冬天傍晚，医院门口的灯已经亮起，排队的队伍沿石阶往下。The hospital is the oldest institution in the town.
sceneCN: 这里 institution 是「机构」（第 1 个义项：大学、医院等大型组织），句意是这家医院是镇上最古老的机构。画面里能看到的物件：石阶、石柱、铜牌、灯。

pos.zh: 名词：机构；制度；由来已久的做法

derivatives.zh: 本词所对应的动词与名词，义为「设立；研究所」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「机构的；制度性的」
由 institutional 加 -ize 构成，义为「制度化」
由 institutionalize 加 -d 构成，义为「已制度化的」

senses.title: An organisation
senses.definition: a large organisation set up for a public or professional purpose, such as a bank or a university
senses.definitionCN: 为公共或专业目的建立的大型组织，如银行或大学
senses.example: The museum is a public institution and entrance is free.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆是公共机构，免费入场。
senses.why: Latin instituere "to set up" gives the result noun: something set up and standing on its own.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instituere「设立」给出结果名词：被设立起来、独立存在的东西。

senses.title: An established custom
senses.titleCN: 由来已久的习俗与制度
senses.definition: a custom or practice that a society has long accepted and rarely questions
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会长期接受、很少质疑的习俗或做法
senses.example: The Sunday dinner is an institution in that family.
senses.exampleCN: 星期日聚餐在那个家庭里是雷打不动的惯例。
senses.why: A practice set up long ago and never taken down is felt as a thing standing there.
senses.whyCN: 很久以前设立、从未撤下的做法，会被感受为一件一直立在那里的事物。

senses.title: A place for care
senses.definition: a building where people are cared for over long periods, often used in older writing
senses.definitionCN: 长期照料人的场所，旧文常用此说法
senses.example: The old building was once an institution for orphaned children.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋旧楼曾是收容孤儿的机构。
senses.why: Buildings set up to keep and care for people took the general word for a set-up place.
senses.whyCN: 为收容和照料人而设立的场所沿用了「设立之处的通称」。

intro.en: Institution is the Latin noun of result from instituere "to set up", literally "something that has been set up".
intro.cn: institution 是拉丁语 instituere「设立」的结果名词，字面是「被设立起来的东西」。

items.en: Statuere "to make stand" and instituere "to set up" are both classical.
items.cn: statuere「使站立」与 instituere「设立」都是古典拉丁语词汇。

items.en: The noun institutio named the act of setting up or of teaching.
items.cn: 名词 institutio 指设立的行为或教导。

items.en: Old French institution passed into Middle English with both meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 institution 连同两层含义进入中古英语。

items.en: The eighteenth and nineteenth centuries made it the general word for social bodies.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪它成为社会组织的通称。

items.en: Modern sociology uses it for customs and norms as well as buildings.
items.cn: 现代社会学用它兼指建筑与习俗规范。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -stitut- stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for organisations and customs.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -stitut- 词干；近义组收其他表示「组织」与「习俗」的词。

entries.definition: A research body, or the verb meaning to set one up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「研究所」，动词义为「设立」。

entries.definition: The framework of rules that constitutes a state.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宪法」，构成国家的规则框架。

entries.definition: The act of putting one thing in place of another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「替换」。

entries.definition: Any structured group, without the sense of long establishment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「组织」，不强调历史久远。

entries.definition: A usual practice, close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「习俗」，与第 2 义近义。

entries.definition: A group with a formal purpose, a bare synonym in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「团体」，正式文体中可同义替换。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the word to its verb and to the buildings and customs it names.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把本词与它的动词以及它所命名的建筑、习俗联系起来。

normal.en: institute plus -ion: something set up and now standing.
normal.cn: institute 加 -ion：设立起来、如今站立的东西。

normal.en: Banks, hospitals and schools are all institutions.
normal.cn: 银行、医院、学校都是 institution。

normal.en: Institutional reform changes the rules, not the walls.
normal.cn: institutional reform 改的是规则，不是墙。

normal.en: A weekly dinner can be an institution too.
normal.cn: 每周一次的家庭聚餐也可以是一种惯例。

normal.en: Institutionalized people have lived long inside such places.
normal.cn: institutionalized 形容人长期生活在机构之中。

abstract.en: Institutions are habits with stone walls around them.
abstract.cn: 制度是围上了石墙的习惯。

abstract.en: A phrase becomes an institution once nobody remembers inventing it.
abstract.cn: 当一个说法没人记得是谁发明的，它就成了惯例。

abstract.en: Institutions are slow to change and slow to fall.
abstract.cn: 机构改变得慢，崩塌也慢。

examples.en: The bank is a respected financial institution.
examples.cn: 这家银行是受人尊敬的金融机构。

examples.en: Marriage is a social institution that varies by culture.
examples.cn: 婚姻是一种因文化而异的社会制度。

examples.en: They campaigned for institutional reform.
examples.cn: 他们为制度改革而奔走。

root: 拉丁语 statuere「使站立」→ instituere「设立」→ 名词 institutio「设立；教导」→ 古法语 institution → 中古英语。与 institute、constitute、substitute 同族，现代社会学用其指制度与习俗。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a formal organisation, a long-accepted custom, and an older word for a care home.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：正式组织、长期被接受的习俗，以及旧时指照料机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stone steps, pillars and an old wooden door with a brass nameplate.
core.cn: 核心意象：石阶、石柱与刻着名字的旧木门。

branches.en: THE DOORPLATE: a bank, a school, a museum.
branches.cn: 门牌这条线：银行、学校、博物馆。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR: a habit repeated until it is a rule.
branches.cn: 日历这条线：重复成规则的习俗。

branches.en: THE WARD: a place where people are cared for over years.
branches.cn: 病房这条线：长期照料人的场所。

branches.en: THE LINK: buildings and customs share the idea of an accepted arrangement.
branches.cn: 连接线：建筑与习俗共享「被接受的安排」这一观念。

branches.en: THE TONE: the care sense today sounds old or institutional.
branches.cn: 语气线：照料义如今显得陈旧或冷硬。

intro.en: Institution is in- plus the Latin stem statu- "set standing", with the noun ending -io.
intro.cn: institution 是 in- 加拉丁词干 statu-「使站立」，再加名词词尾 -io。

latinIntro.en: Latin instituere and institutio are both recorded, so this layer is fully attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instituere 与 institutio 均有记载，这一层完全有据。
